subject: design-technology
title: Foundations of Materials & Manufacturing
welcome_lead: Step into the workshop and meet the six material families and the four scales of production that shape every product around you.
meta_desc: Learn material categories and scales of production for GCSE Design & Technology.
final_note: You can now sort materials by family and match production scales to product demand.

concepts.def: Natural material from trees, including hardwoods and softwoods.
Synthetic material made from oil, often called plastic.
Making a single bespoke product, often by hand.
Making a set number of identical items in groups.
Continuous large-scale making of identical products.

walkthroughs.body_html: GCSE D&T groups materials into six families: timbers (oak, pine), metals (steel, aluminium), polymers (HDPE, acrylic), textiles (cotton, polyester), papers and boards (cartridge, corrugated), and electronic/mechanical components (resistors, gears). Each family has unique working properties that suit different products.

A bespoke wedding ring uses one-off production. A run of 500 school chairs is batch. Millions of identical phones come from mass production. Steel sheet rolled non-stop in a mill is continuous. The scale depends on demand, cost and how unique each item is.
A toy company sells 10,000 wooden cars per month. One-off is too slow and continuous would overproduce. Mass production on an assembly line matches the volume and keeps unit cost low.

It is the cheapest method for any quantity.
